acceptance.criterion_verbatim: ONE-TO-ONE BY MINTED ID, NOTHING INVENTED: per-part join line (card or no card / ambiguous / unjoined); admission strictly by the ratified registry + the key predicate.
acceptance.output_evidence: 26 JOINED | 16 UNJOINED | 0 AMBIGUOUS = 42 of 42, one printed line per part. No part matched more than one member, so nothing was picked between candidates. Admission is strictly by the RATIFIED registry: the runner REFUSES outright when ratified_at_commit is null, because an unratified registry cannot supply registry-ratified members. THE JOIN KEY IS A NAMED GAP AND WAS NOT INVENTED: no registry-MINTED part id exists (members carry path/git_blob_id/subject_id; parts carry a path-string id), which 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X had already recorded. Two readings differ by 26 rows -- (a) literal, 0 of 42; (b) operative, exact match against a ratified subject_id. Implemented (b) on the textual argument that (a) makes the arm's own clause 'leave string-name misses unjoined' VACUOUS; RULED (b) OPERATIVE by 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X 011930Z. Both counts print on every run so the other reading needs no re-run.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: TWO NUMBERS, PERMANENT UNKNOWNS INSIDE: EMISSION and DECLARATION printed against one denominator; the three by-construction parts named inside unknown.
acceptance.output_evidence: EMISSION 42 of 42 -- every part carries all four receivers (grain, key, failure_mode, home_space) with a coherent claim_status. DECLARATION 0 declared / 42 unknown. Two numbers against the ONE denominator 42, never summarised into a rate and never reported alone (PRD 10.2). A BARE ZERO IS NOT A FINDING UNTIL IT SAYS WHAT IT IS ZERO OF, so the per-receiver split prints: grain / key / failure_mode read claim_status 'unknown' on 42 of 42, and home_space is a bare string carrying no claim_status at all. Emission is a SHAPE claim the manifest fully satisfies; declaration is a KNOWLEDGE claim it makes nowhere -- and nothing in this round changed that, because the keyfill declared the CARDS' key_expression, not the MANIFEST's part.key. THE THREE PERMANENTLY UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION are named FROM THE PRD rather than derived by a predicate: affinity_matrix, identity_and_succession, similarity_network_fusion -- 3 of 3 present, all unjoined, all L2/L3/L4 unbuilt destinations, and NOT DEBT.

mutant.description: The join's admission gate and its key discipline, each exercised against the state that should stop them: a registry with ratified_at_commit null must refuse; a part whose id is not VERBATIM a ratified subject_id must land in unjoined rather than being basename-matched or fuzzed into a join.
mutant.expected: an unratified registry refuses outright; near-miss names stay unjoined; a part with two candidates reads AMBIGUOUS, stays unknown and prints both, while the same part with one candidate reads JOINED
mutant.observed: 16 of 42 parts are UNJOINED on exactly that rule, including names a fuzzy matcher would have joined (graph_edges, graph_nodes, cse, code_heat_snap). The ratified-registry gate is a hard return before any join runs. ON AMBIGUOUS, A DEFECT 4.0.0_SA_CRO~X FOUND AND I HAD MIS-DESCRIBED: the subject index was a DICT, so duplicate subject_ids collapsed before the hit count and the AMBIGUOUS branch was UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- its 0 was a property of the data structure, not of the population, and would have read 0 on a registry that DID carry duplicates. I had called it 'not exercised on this population', which was too kind: it could not be exercised on ANY population. Replaced with a multimap. The required two-candidate MUTANT now runs every time, PAIRED WITH ITS SINGLE-CANDIDATE POSITIVE CONTROL on the same subject: the real registry gives that part 1 candidate -> JOINED; a copy of the member list carrying one extra member with the same subject_id gives it 2 -> AMBIGUOUS, both candidates PRINTED and neither picked, with the rest of the population unchanged. THE TWO ARMS DIFFER IN ONE FACT AND RUN THROUGH THE SAME index_members()/classify() AS THE LIVE JOIN -- a control that re-implements the logic it tests only proves the bug can be written twice, and a hand-computed length would have 'passed' against the dict as well. The mutant is a REFUSAL arm, not a print: a run whose mutant fails to reach AMBIGUOUS returns 1. THAT ARM WAS ITSELF EXERCISED rather than declared -- restoring the exact dict-collapse defect in memory drives the run to exit 1 on 'REFUSING: the two-candidate mutant did not reach AMBIGUOUS', so both halves are reachable from different truths. With the branch live, the population's own count is 0 registry subject_ids carrying more than one member -- consistent with the ratified compile's exact-duplicate count of 0, and now a measurement rather than an artifact. The ratified registry bytes were not touched: the injection is into a new list.

determinism.method: the join re-run against the same ratified registry and the same manifest; every count derived at run time from the two artifacts, none typed
determinism.observed: identical on repeat: 26 / 16 / 0 over 42, EMISSION 42, DECLARATION 0/42, L0 PASS. The reconciliation joined + unjoined + ambiguous == denominator is asserted by the runner and its exit code depends on it.

declared_exclusions.item: joining the 16 unjoined parts by any means other than an exact ratified subject_id
declared_exclusions.reason: the arm forbids it and the alternative is inventing a correspondence. Several would join under a basename or prefix rule; that is precisely the string-name miss the clause names, and a wrong join is worse than an absent one because it is invisible downstream.

declared_exclusions.item: minting a part id to close the join-key gap
declared_exclusions.reason: 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X recorded the member-grain id as a named gap, never to be invented. Closing it is a contract act for the design lane, not an executor's convenience.

declared_exclusions.item: the 3 permanently-unknown parts' absence from the join
declared_exclusions.reason: affinity_matrix, identity_and_succession and similarity_network_fusion are this arc's own unbuilt L2/L3/L4 destinations. The PRD states they are not debt and that any count treating them as outstanding is reading the wrong thing; they are named in the output rather than dropped.

declared_exclusions.item: raising DECLARATION by declaring manifest receivers
declared_exclusions.reason: out of this TO's scope and out of this seat's authority for most of them. The keyfill declared the CARDS' key_expression; the MANIFEST's part.key remains a source gap the PRD already names.

surprises: OBSERVATION / DISARMED -- there is no registry-MINTED part id on either side of the join, so the arm's key had two readings differing by 26 rows. Both counted and printed on every run; 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X ruled the operative reading at 011930Z.

OBSERVATION / DISARMED -- my first EMISSION and DECLARATION predicates were invented ('a part with a home', 'claim_status == declared') and both returned 42 of 42: the right SHAPE from the wrong RULE, which is the agreement most likely to survive review. Reading D11_SUBSTRATE_ANALYSIS_PRD.md 10.2 at source gave 42 and 0.

OBSERVATION / DISARMED -- the compiler NULLS ratified_at_commit by construction, so re-running it after ratification would silently un-ratify the registry. Flagged to the ratifier at 80049 as a live hazard in the tool's current shape rather than left to be discovered.

OBSERVATION / DISARMED -- the AMBIGUOUS branch was UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: a dict keyed on subject_id collapsed duplicates before the hit count, so its 0 was a property of the data structure and would have read 0 even on a registry carrying duplicates. Found by 4.0.0_SA_CRO~X at the exact line. Replaced with a multimap; a two-candidate mutant now proves the branch reachable on every run, after which the population's own 0 duplicates is a measurement.
